title: They didn’t tell you this…
paragraphs:
The reason you’re being targeted
…is not because you’re weak.
It’s because you’re carrying something the enemy is terrified of.
There are nights you don’t even recognize yourself anymore.

You love God…
but your thoughts betray you.

You worship…
but your habits still haunt you.

You smile in public…
but privately, you’re fighting battles you’re too ashamed to name.
Let me say what most won’t:
You’re in a war over your identity.
Because the enemy knows something you keep forgetting—

If he can keep you trapped in shame…
he can keep you silent.

If he can keep you hiding…
he can keep you powerless.

If he can keep you believing “this is just who I am”…
he can stop you from becoming who God called you to be.

"You’re still the same."
"God is tired of you."
"Real Christians don’t struggle like this."
“There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.” — Romans 8:1

Because there’s a difference between what God declared
and what you’ve believed.

Some scholars interpret this passage as a legal declaration—
that in Christ, your guilt is completely removed before God.

Others emphasize the relational side—
that you are not just forgiven, but fully accepted as a child.
So why does shame still feel so loud?
Because the enemy is not trying to rewrite heaven’s verdict.
He’s trying to distort your perception of it.
Because instead of running to God when you fall—
That’s where the real damage happens.
But in the distance that follows.
You didn’t plan to be here.
That cycle you swore you’d break last year.
You said, “This is the last time.”
And now shame is louder than your faith.

"Maybe I’m not really saved."
"Maybe I’ve gone too far this time."
"Maybe God is done with me."
That is not the voice of your Shepherd.
Because Jesus never pushes sinners away.
“Come to me, all who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.” — Matthew 11:28
But here’s where it gets deeper—
Jesus doesn’t just invite you to rest.
“Try harder and maybe you’ll be accepted.”
“You were dead in sin… and Jesus died to bring you back to life.”
“But God shows his love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” — Romans 5:8
While you were still in it.
Every moment you’d be too ashamed to tell anyone.
And He still chose the cross.
The nails were not a reaction to your perfection.
They were a response to your brokenness.
He wasn’t just ending His suffering.
So why are you still living like you owe something?
Why are you still punishing yourself for what Jesus already paid for?
And I say that with love—
You think staying in shame proves you’re sorry.
But all it does is keep you stuck.
Shame drives you away from Him.
If he can keep you isolated…
But here’s the truth he hopes you never fully grasp:
You are not fighting for victory.
Grace is not permission to stay in sin.
It’s power to come out of it.
“What shall we say then? Are we to continue in sin that grace may abound? By no means!” — Romans 6:1–2
But you have to step into it.
Because the longer you stay in the dark—
But the moment you bring it into the light—
“If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.” — 1 John 1:9
So what are you still holding onto?
That version of yourself God already nailed to the cross?
Whisper it if you have to:
But now you won’t fight alone.
Because the same Jesus who died for you—

So the next time the enemy whispers,
"You’re still the same…"
If this spoke directly to your heart—
